title: Propositional normal forms: truth functions and complete connectives
summary: Build formulas from truth-table rows, obtain disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms, and express every finite truth function with small connective bases.
abstract: A lamp controlled by two switches might be required to light exactly when their settings differ. A truth table records this requirement, and a propositional formula can express it. The same is true of every table with finitely many inputs: combine the rows where the output is true, or exclude the rows where it is false. These constructions put every formula into disjunctive and conjunctive normal form, though the resulting formula need not be short or unique. They also show that small choices of connectives suffice to express every finite truth function, provided we specify which constants are available.
